articles.title: Revised lower to 2.0%
articles.heading: Norwegian unemployment
articles.fulltext:
The seasonal-adjusted registered jobless rate was stable at 2.0% in September, after a downward adjustment of the August numbers. Unemployment is thus running marginally below Norges Bank’s 2.1% estimate. However, data overall continue to point to a stable and healthy labour market, in line with Norges Bank’s reasoning in the Sep MPR.
Registered unemployment: 
The unadjusted jobless rate fell 0.1ppt to 2.0% in September. The seasonal-adjusted unemployment rate was stable at 2.0%, after a downward revision to the August numbers. The number of fully unemployed persons fell by 642, while people on employment schemes increased resulting in unemployment incl. employment schemes being stable at 2.6% (SA). In unadjusted terms, fully unemployed persons amounted to 59.4k, part-time unemployed 22.9k and people on employment schemes totalled 12.8k. The latter two corresponds to 0.8% and 0.4% of the labour force, respectively.
In September, unemployment was broadly stable across most occupational groups, with the largest increase in engineering and ICT. Unemployment in these fields has risen over the past year though from a low level, and NAV reports that part of the increase is due to the petroleum sector. Unemployment is highest in travel and transport (3.5%), and lowest among professionals (1.0%) and health and care workers (1.1%).
New registered job vacancies were 44.5k in September, which was 3% higher than a year ago. Vacancies were highest within health care followed by the retail sector and service occupations. New registered job vacancies tend to be volatile on a monthly basis, but overall, it points to still healthy labour demand with the long-term trend moving sideways.
Implications Norges Bank:
 In its Sep MPR, Norges Bank forecasted the registered jobless rate to remain steady at 2.1% for the remainder of the year, rising gradually from Q1 2027 to peak at 2.4% in mid-2028. Due to the revision of the August numbers, unemployment is running 0.1ppt below Norges Bank’s forecast. However, we do not expect this to be decisive for whether Norges Bank delivers another rate hike or not. The overall picture is that unemployment and new registered job vacancies are stable, which is in line with Norges Bank’s view from the Sep MPR.

articles.title: US payrolls, gloom ahead of Sunday's Brazil election
articles.heading: Nordic Alert
articles.fulltext:
Global key stories
U.S. Treasury yields fell back slightly on Thursday after hitting new highs but the 10-year was at 5.34% earlier in the day. That in turn led to some breathing room for the stock market (S&P 500 +0.2%; Nasdaq unchanged) despite yesterday's higher oil price. Treasury yields have been pushed upwards due to concerns about high inflation, and the development of energy costs. A possible escalation in the conflict between Washington and Tehran will be crucial for whether the recovery for US government bonds can continue. The stock market in Asia is heading for its worst week since July and the stock market in Europe is heading towards its worst since April.
Nonfarm payrolls and European inflation in focus.
 Today's US employment report can provide clues about what will be required of the Fed's interest rate policy. The focus today will also be on euro area inflation for September. In addition, data on unemployment in Norway and Spain, Brazilian and South Korean inflation and Russian GDP will be released. Japan's core inflation in September came in at 3% year-on-year. This was significantly higher than analysts' expectations but may have been affected by an unusually long weekend period (the so-called "silver week") that temporarily drove up certain price categories.
Gloomy prospects in Brazil's elections
. On Sunday, Brazil will hold the first round of general elections, where opinion polls show a tight race between incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and challenger Flávio Bolsonaro. Over the past half century, Brazil's economy has stagnated both compared to other countries in the region and global average growth. The incumbent left-wing president, Lula, will soon be 81 years old, the same age Joe Biden was when he withdrew his candidacy for re-election in 2024. Despite his commitment to democratic institutions and a healthy attitude to environmental issues, he has failed to stimulate growth and restrain public spending. Apart from a simplification of the sales tax, economic reforms have not materialized. His term ends with the highest government bond yield in 10 years. His opponent, the 45-year-old Bolsonaro, denies that humans are causing climate change, questions democratic institutions such as the electoral process, and suggests that he will not respect the election results if Lula wins. He has been under investigation for alleged links to violent criminals, which he denies. His main political goal is to pardon his father, who was sentenced to 27 years in prison in September 2025 for planning a coup – including a plan to assassinate Lula – after failing to be re-elected president in 2022. Neither candidate appears to offer policies that simultaneously guarantee both democratic rights and more sustainable economic development. 
The French government wants to reduce the budget deficit for 2027 by €43 billion
 through spending cuts and tax increases. 
The plan 
freezes some pension increases and limits pay increases for civil servants, and would mean an adjustment of the deficit from 5.4% of GDP this year to 5% next year. France's public debt is at its highest level since World War II.
Military build-up in the Middle East.
 The U.S. will send more troops, including a 
third aircraft carrier group
, to the Middle East, while President Trump warns that new attacks on Iran could be on the way after the congressional elections in November. In addition
, 
Axios
 reports 
 that the U.S. has sent more anti-aircraft missiles to the Gulf states, with one of the motives reportedly being to reassure countries that energy facilities will be protected if Trump orders new attacks.

articles.title: Amerikansk sysselsättning, dystert läge inför söndagens Brasilien-val
articles.heading: Morning Alert
articles.fulltext:
Internationellt
Amerikanska marknadsräntor föll tillbaka något under torsdagen efter att ha nått nya toppnivåer men 10-åringen på 5,34% tidigare under dagen. Det ledde i sin tur till visst andrum för börsen (S&P 500 +0,2%; Nasdaq oförändrat) trots gårdagens högre oljepris. De amerikanska räntorna har tryckts uppåt pga. oro över den höga inflationen, och utvecklingen av energikostnaderna. En eventuell eskalering i konflikten mellan Washington och Teheran blir avgörande för om återhämtningen för amerikanska statsobligationer kan hålla i sig. Börsen i Asien går mot sin sämsta vecka sedan juli och börsen i Europa mot sin sämsta sedan april.
Amerikansk sysselsättning och europeisk inflation i fokus.
 Dagens amerikanska sysselsättningsrapport (”nonfarm payrolls”) kan ge ledtrådar om vad som kommer krävas av Feds räntepolitik. Fokus idag kommer också ligga på euroområdets inflation för september. Därutöver släpps data på arbetslöshet i Norge och Spanien, brasiliansk respektive sydkoreansk inflation samt rysk BNP. Japans kärninflation i september kom in på 3% i årstakt. Det var betydligt högre än analytikernas förväntningar men kan ha påverkats av en ovanligt lång helgperiod (den s.k. ”silverveckan”) som temporärt drivit upp vissa priskategorier.
Dystra valutsikter i Brasilien
. På söndag håller Brasilien första omgången i de allmänna valen, där det i opinionsundersökningar har varit dött lopp mellan sittande president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva och utmanaren Flávio Bolsonaro. Under det senaste halvseklet har Brasiliens ekonomi, i stället för att ta fart, stagnerat både jämfört med andra länder i regionen och den globala genomsnittliga tillväxten. Den sittande vänsterpresidenten, Lula, fyller snart 81 år, samma ålder som Joe Biden var när han drog tillbaka sin kandidatur för återval 2024. Trots sitt engagemang för demokratiska institutioner samt en sund inställning till miljöfrågor så har han misslyckats med att stimulera tillväxten och hålla tillbaka de offentliga utgifterna. Bortsett från en förenkling av omsättningsskatten har ekonomiska reformer uteblivit. Hans mandatperiod avslutas med den högsta statsobligationsräntan på 10 år. Hans motståndare, den 45-årige Bolsonaro, förnekar att människan orsakar klimatförändringarna, ifrågasätter demokratiska institutioner som t.ex. valprocessen och antyder att han inte kommer att respektera valresultatet om Lula vinner. Han har varit föremål för utredning på grund av påstådda kopplingar till våldsamma brottslingar, vilket han förnekar. Hans främsta politiska mål är att benåda sin far, som i september 2025 dömdes till 27 års fängelse för att ha planerat en kupp – inklusive en plan att mörda Lula – efter att ha misslyckats med att bli omvald till president 2022. Ingen av kandidaterna ser ut att erbjuda en politik som samtidigt garanterar både demokratiska rättigheter och en mer hållbar ekonomisk utveckling. 
Frankrikes regering vill minska budgetunderskottet för 2027 med 43 miljarder euro
 genom utgiftsnedskärningar och skattehöjningar. 
Planen 
innebär att vissa pensionshöjningar fryses och att löneökningarna för statstjänstemän begränsas, och skulle innebära en justering av underskottet från 5,4% av BNP i år till 5% nästa år. Frankrikes statsskuld ligger på den högsta nivån sedan andra världskriget.
Militär uppladdning i Mellanöstern.
 USA kommer att skicka mer trupper inklusive en 
tredje hangarfartygsgrupp
 till Mellanöstern, samtidigt som president Trump varnar för att nya attacker mot Iran kan vara på väg efter kongressvalet i november. Dessutom rapporterar 
Axios
 att USA skickat fler luftvärnsmissiler till Gulfstaterna, där ett av motiven ska ha varit att försäkra länderna om att energianläggningar kommer att skyddas ifall Trump beordrar nya attacker.

articles.title: Higher for longer priced in
articles.heading: SEB FI & FX Strategy
articles.fulltext:
At a glance:
In market focus.
 Oil and the Middle East; Inflation data; Long-end yields; France.
Global macro and risk appetite. 
Global bond yields have risen sharply in recent weeks, with the 10Y Treasury yield at a two-decade high. Equities have so far proved resilient, while credit has been under pressure since September. Strategically, the most damaging transmission channel from rates to risk appetite is a rise in interest rates large enough to slow GDP growth sharply. Neither the level of bond yields nor rates volatility looks high enough yet to threaten a significant slowdown, but there are warning signals for a possible equity correction. Bond yields have been moving in sync with oil prices, and positioning is heavily skewed towards higher yields. A reopening of the Strait of Hormuz or weaker macro data could therefore trigger a move lower in yields. We think risk assets are unlikely to move higher until the uptrend in rates is broken.
US macro: Strong growth, inflation relief.
 The underlying inflation trend is looking better after the larger than expected downward effect from revised methods for core PCE. Annualized monthly change in line with the target over the past three months has eased the pressure for another near-term rate increase. However, strong growth – with upward revisions to total GDP, firm underlying demand in Q2 and strong spending in August – support that current policy is not restrictive and raises risks for companies passing through rising energy costs to consumers. AI build-out is seen by most of the Fed as a near-term upside risk to both growth and inflation. Rising real yields pose new downside risks for growth and especially through any adverse equity market reactions, given the importance of positive wealth effects for consumers. Markets are pricing less than a 40% probability for an October rate hike (9bp) and a full rate hike in December – which we see as reasonable – followed by two to three additional hikes in 2027 – which we see as excessive.
USD short rates: Waiting for new impetus. 
Terminal SOFR has risen by around 185bp, to 4.85%, since the Iran conflict began at the end of February, and the past week has shown tentative signs of stabilisation. We think policy rate expectations have risen enough for now and see scope for consolidation, with markets waiting for a trigger for the next move.
USD bonds: Higher for longer increasingly priced in.
 The 10Y Treasury yield is above 5.30% after a sharp sell off, driven mainly by higher policy rate expectations, not inflation expectations or term premium. Fed pricing and market positioning are stretched, but the sell off needs a catalyst to fade. Conflict de-escalation or weaker growth data may be the likely triggers, and a correction lower in long yields could be rapid once momentum turns.
France: Rising fiscal concern.
 PM Lecornu's government presented its 2027 draft budget on 1 October, ahead of formal submission on 6 October. Large savings needs and opposition discontent threaten the minority government, while fiscal worries and a lack of reforms are pushing French yields higher. Next year's presidential election adds uncertainty, with candidates at both political extremes gaining in the polls (read more 
here
).
EUR short rates: Policy rate pricing looks complete for now.
 Forwards discounting more than 80bp of additional hikes by next autumn, and we think it will be hard for markets to push pricing materially further at this point. At the same time, markets are likely to resist pricing fewer than 75bp of hikes without a decisive breakthrough that brings a substantial, sustained decline in energy prices.
EUR bonds: France in focus. 
With short positioning stretched and ECB and Fed pricing sufficiently aggressive to account for inflation prospects, we maintain our base case that the 10Y Bund yield will trade predominantly in a 3.40-3.60% range in the near term. The rapid widening of OAT vs. Bund spreads looks concerning and is increasingly spilling over to other markets, but it is unlikely to affect ECB actions materially just yet.
EURUSD: Market already short, but the downside risk is growing.
 The wider US–EUR 2Y differential has driven EURUSD lower, but that driver now looks close to exhausted: US policy pricing is stretched and positioning is skewed toward higher yields. The market is also already short EURUSD, which helps explain why spot has held up better than the backdrop suggests. The risk has shifted lower over the past week, though. French stress is spreading to Italy and Spain, and options are pricing more protection against a weaker euro. A sustained break below support would confirm that the euro-area premium is reaching FX and open 1.10–1.11. The upside risk is a positioning-driven squeeze.
Forecasts. 
Links to SEB’s official 
macro
, 
central bank
 and 
financial
 forecasts.
USD bonds: Higher for longer increasingly priced in
Two weeks ago, we expected the 10Y Treasury yield to consolidate in the 4.90-5.10% range. With the 10Y now trading above 5.30%, our view of consolidation proved premature. We see yields as stretched, but the sell off needs a catalyst to fade, most likely conflict de-escalation or weaker growth data.
Pricing of rate hikes through end-2027 has risen by around 185bp in the US and 125bp in the euro area versus levels prevailing just before the Iran conflict escalated at the end of February. As argued in the previous SEB FI & FX Strategy, policy rate expectations have reached a level where markets will likely struggle to push them much further without new triggers. Any further rise in yields would therefore more likely have to come from a higher term premium, which has so far remained contained. Conversely, with an already aggressive policy path priced in and positioning heavily skewed towards higher yields, better prospects for conflict de-escalation or disappointing growth data could trigger a rapid unwinding of part of the discounted hikes and a correction lower in long yields.
Cumulative rate hikes from inception of the Iran conflict to end-2027 discounted by futures: Fed and ECB
Policy rate expectations remain the key driver. 
The rise in the 10Y Treasury yield has continued to track policy rate expectations (illustrated by the 3Y forward on the 1M SOFR rate in the chart below), in line with our conclusion on the Bund yield in the previous report.
Policy rate expectations (SOFR) and 10Y Treasury yield
Long US rates have tracked oil prices closely since the start of the conflict until recently. Since mid-September, however, yields have kept rising, despite some pullback in oil. The deviation probably reflects higher-for-longer policy rate expectations, but we think developments that bring oil prices lower would help to ease pressure on bond markets.
Oil prices and 10Y Treasury yield
Inflation expectations remain anchored. 
Despite higher oil and other commodity prices, long-term inflation expectations are well anchored. Both 10Y and 5Y5Y CPI swaps trade at the levels seen in February. The 10Y real rate, however, has climbed from around 1.15% at the end of February to nearly 2.40% currently. A substantial repricing of the policy path (higher for longer) combined with stable inflation expectations suggests markets trust the Fed's commitment to its inflation target.
Inflation expectations (10Y CPI swap) and 10Y real rate (SOFR-CPI swap), %
Term premium up only modestly since the conflict began. 
The term premium has trended higher in recent years, as investors demand greater compensation for holding long-duration Treasuries amid uncertainty over inflation and the Fed's policy path, fiscal supply, long-term debt sustainability, and a marginal buyer base shifting towards more price-sensitive investors. The Fed's ACM model, the measure most widely followed by markets, has moved broadly sideways since mid-2025 and risen only modestly since the end of February. It supports the view that the rise in yields has been driven mainly by higher-for-longer policy rate expectations.
US: Term premium in 10Y tenor according to the ACM and Kim&Wright models
Structural term premium risks skewed higher. 
The term premium in Treasury yields is still relatively low in a long-term perspective, and we see risks skewed towards a structural increase in the coming years. Investors are likely to demand higher compensation for duration, particularly if the hedging qualities of Treasuries against shocks are seen weakening, for example on (geo)political or structural grounds.
US: Term premium in 10Y tenor, long-term perspective
Even with a structural rise in term premium, other factors will likely matter more for Treasury yields over the next 6-12 months, notably inflation and growth prospects, which in turn hinge on conflict resolution. With positioning stretched, a correction lower could be rapid once upside momentum fades. Historically, however, a sustained decline in long yields has emerged only near the end of hiking cycles.
EURUSD: Market already short, but downside risks are growing.
 The wider US–euro-area two-year differential has driven EURUSD lower, but further US policy repricing looks increasingly difficult to sustain. European fiscal stress is becoming the more important downside risk. French spreads have widened sharply, Italy and Spain have begun to follow, and options are pricing more expensive protection against a weaker euro. Short CTA positioning leaves room for a squeeze, but we need to give weight to the risk that fiscal stress broadens and puts further pressure on EURUSD. A sustained break below support, accompanied by broader European stress, would open the way towards 1.10–1.11.
The rate differential has driven EURUSD lower, but that driver looks increasingly mature.
 Since the Iran conflict escalated, the implied end-2027 US rate has risen by around 185bp, compared with roughly 125bp in the euro area. The larger US repricing has widened the two-year differential and weighed on EURUSD. As argued in the USD rates section, however, US policy pricing looks stretched and positioning is skewed towards higher yields. A further sell-off increasingly requires a fresh catalyst, while additional upward pressure on long yields may come from term premium rather than policy expectations.
The risks to the differential are therefore becoming more two-sided. We see the hawkish US repricing as excessive, while ECB expectations may remain sticky unless energy prices fall decisively. A correction driven by softer US data could narrow the differential and support EURUSD. That would weaken one source of downward pressure on the pair, but would not necessarily offset a growing European fiscal risk premium
Fiscal stress is broadening across the euro area, although markets are still differentiating.
 OAT–Bund widening has been accompanied by a sharp rise in French CDS and French equity underperformance. Italy has followed, and Spain has now widened too. France remains under the greatest pressure and Spain the least, suggesting that investors are still distinguishing between sovereign risks. Nevertheless, the widening beyond France raises the risk that fiscal concerns become a broader euro-area problem.
Part of the move has tracked the global rise in long-end yields, led by US Treasuries. Higher financing costs amplify fiscal vulnerabilities, and a turn lower in US yields could therefore ease some pressure. If French spreads fail to narrow alongside that relief, it would strengthen the case that domestic fiscal concerns are sustaining the repricing.
For EURUSD, the escalation test is whether peripheral widening exceeds what global yields and the usual relationships with France would explain, and whether European banks begin to underperform. Those developments would strengthen the case that sovereign stress is becoming an independent driver of euro weakness.
EURUSD’s resilience is increasingly vulnerable to broader fiscal stress.
 Spot has weakened, but has not shown the same degree of stress as French sovereign markets. Our CTA proxy already indicates short EURUSD positioning, which may dampen additional selling from trend-following investors and leaves the pair exposed to short covering. FX may also still be treating French spread widening partly as an extension of the global rates move.
We see a growing risk that this resilience is challenged. The French spread to Bunds is at its widest since the euro-area debt crisis. Although it remains below the 2012 peak and does not imply the same systemic risks, the scale and speed of the repricing warrant attention. Italy and Spain beginning to follow increases the risk that the pressure extends beyond France. Existing shorts may slow the adjustment, but do not provide a floor if the underlying outlook deteriorates.
Protection is building in both directions, but most of all against a weaker euro.
 Implied vol has risen across the curve, lifting the cost of hedging both a stronger and a weaker EUR, so the market is pricing larger moves either way. The put side has led, though. One-month 10-delta put vol has jumped from around 5.5 to 8, and in 1Y, put vol has risen to its highest level in a year while the premium over at-the-money has widened. The market is not just hedging a break in the range: it is starting to pay for a more persistent EUR downside, while keeping upside convexity on the table.
Energy: still a risk, but with room for optimism. 
With the injection season over and the threat of a US diesel export ban receding, near-term energy pressure on Europe may ease. Winter and next year's refill season remain tight, so the risk has not gone away, but it is less likely to be the trigger for EUR weakness.
The downside risk for EURUSD has grown over the past week.
 French stress has spread to Italy and Spain, spot is testing the bottom of its 2026 range, and options are pricing more protection against a weaker euro. But positioning remains stretched, so the upside has not gone away.
Scenarios:
Downside: French stress reaching FX.
 The main downside risk is euro-area fiscal stress spreading beyond France. Watch for spreads widening beyond the move in global yields, together with European banks underperforming. In a market this short positioned, and but a sustained break lower, breaking resistant levels, would open 1.10–1.11. Even if there have been some energy relief, a persistent winter premium would still reinforce a break.
Upside, short term: a positioning-driven squeeze.
 The most likely upside trigger is US yields peaking. As argued in the USD rates section, policy pricing looks stretched and positioning is skewed toward higher yields. With more hikes priced in the US than in the euro area, a correction would likely narrow the 2Y differential, and short positions in Treasuries and EURUSD could unwind together. A manageable outcome to the French budget votes on 20 October and 17 November, together with easing diesel stress, would remove two euro-area brakes. That could lift EURUSD back above 1.15. Because the rally would be driven by positioning rather than fundamentals, we would treat it as a correction, not a turn.
Upside, longer term: disinflation and conflict resolution.
 A sustained EUR recovery needs global disinflation that lets markets lower rate expectations, that would most likely follow from an end to the conflict that brings oil prices down. That is more likely a 2027 story than a Q4 one.

articles.title: Ahead of September CPI
articles.heading: Swedish inflation
articles.fulltext:
Slightly higher core inflation in September
CPIF ex energy
 is predicted to increase to 0.7% y/y in September (August 0.5% y/y, Riksbank forecast: 0.7% y/y). 
CPIF 
is seen increasing markedly to 1.6% y/y (August 0.7% y/y Riksbank: 1.5% y/y), from 0.7% y/y last month. Both electricity and fuel prices rose sharply in September.
CPIF ex energy
 corrected for lower VAT and higher subsidy for public transport is expected to edge higher to 1.6% y/y in September (August 1.5% y/y, Riksbank forecast 1.8% y/y).
Gradually rising inflation from modest levels 
September is the first monthly reading after the September Monetary Policy report (MPR). The forecast for CPIF ex energy was largely unchanged compared to the June MPR. We predict core inflation to trend gradually higher over the next 6 months driven by a weaker SEK and expect some indirect effects from higher energy prices. The forecast for CPIF ex energy has been revised slightly higher due to upward revisions to the forecasts for rents in apartments and co-ops. Earlier and larger rate hikes from the Riksbank will exert upward pressure on rents. 
So far, near-term indicators, such as pricing plans and producer prices on consumer goods, have remained low; this is the case both in Sweden and in the euro area. Prices on package holidays, car rentals and hotels increased more than normal during the summer and price levels continue to be elevated, despite falling back in August. A continued normalisation is a downside risk to CPIF ex energy in September. 
Sharply higher energy prices in September. 
Fuel prices are set to rise by 14% and electricity prices by 9% m/m in September, driven by higher market prices. A reversal of temporary tax reductions on fuels means that energy prices will continue to rise sharply in Q4. Futures pricing indicate large price drops on both electricity and fuels over the next 6-12 months, but the decline has been delayed. Headline CPIF will rise well above the target in the beginning of next year, although the inflation rate will be very volatile. 
Policy implications
The Riksbank was more hawkish than expected in September and the meeting minutes confirmed that the probability for a rate hike in November is very high. None of the Board members discussed the possibility of hiking in both November and December, but this is the main scenario implied by current market pricing. We stick to our forecast for rate hikes in November, February and May and some recent retracing of aggressive market-implied expectations for near-term rate hikes from the ECB and the Fed supports our forecast. After the notable shift in policy stance in September, uncertainty has increased. Actual inflation, developments in the Middle East, as well as foreign central banks will decide the size and the timing of rate hikes.

articles.title: Long rates continue higher – despite oil below USD 100
articles.heading: Nordic Alert
articles.fulltext:
Global key stories
US long rates continued higher yesterday.
 The 10-year yield is now very close to breaking above its highest level since the financial crisis, a milestone the 30-year yield already passed on Tuesday. The rise came despite inflation, as measured by the Fed’s preferred gauge, PCE, coming in below expectations and the market subsequently pricing a slightly lower probability of a rate hike in October. Long rates instead took greater cue from growth data that reinforced the picture of surprisingly resilient US growth in the first half of the year.
Equity markets were somewhat mixed, with tech-heavy Nasdaq edging higher while the S&P 500 declined. In Europe, country-level inflation data suggest that the 2.5% core inflation forecast may hold, although there is some risk of an upside surprise. Attention therefore shifts to growth, with PMIs for many countries and the US ISM on today’s agenda.
In Asia, equity markets that are open are generally higher, but note that Chinese markets are closed today and will remain closed until next Thursday owing to the National Day holiday. Equity futures point to a lower open in Europe but a higher open in the US.
Oil prices fell sharply overnight to USD 97 per barrel, without yet generating major headlines. According to 
Bloomberg
, attention has shifted towards oil flows out of the Middle East approaching pre-war levels, although it remains unclear whether quarterly effects may also be affecting the price.
Will the US ISM manufacturing index confirm last week’s strong PMI?
 Last week’s surprise rise in September PMI readings, to their highest levels in several years, was interpreted as further evidence of the surprisingly strong resilience of the US economy. However, we do not expect today’s ISM manufacturing index, released at 16:00 CET, to show a similar increase. Instead, the index is expected to be broadly unchanged, albeit at still solid levels. A decline in several regional manufacturing surveys in September also poses a downside risk. Beyond the headline figure, the ISM will be closely scrutinised for signs of renewed bottlenecks in prices and delivery times, in line with signals from both the PMI and several regional indices.
September and Q3 market wrap.
 With both September and the third quarter now behind us, both periods were characterised by higher oil prices and rates, a stronger dollar and a weaker krona. US equities, however, rose over the third quarter, even though they declined in September (see table below). One possible explanation is that the bulk of the move in rates did not occur until September, which also pushed yields to levels that are more challenging for equities.
In FX (charts below), high-yielding currencies outperformed in the third quarter while low-yielding currencies underperformed – a clear sign that carry trades dominated. One exception was the low-yielding JPY, which was supported by repeated interventions.
Nordic key stories
Riksbank minutes confirm the hawkish shift.
 The minutes confirm the hawkish shift from last week’s rate decision, but also show that views on the balance of risks still differ within the Executive Board. A rate hike in November looks highly likely, with further hikes expected next year. However, board members remain vague on the pace and extent of additional increases. The global outlook will be crucial, and energy prices remain an important factor for the rate outlook. We still expect rate hikes in November, February and May. Read more 
here
.
Recovery in Swedish manufacturing PMI.
 The September PMI is released at 08:30 CET, and we expect the index to show a recovery. This would see the PMI continue to reverse part of July’s unexpected decline, when the index fell after an upward trend since 2023.

articles.title: Långräntorna fortsätter upp – trots oljepris under 100 dollar
articles.heading: Morning Alert
articles.fulltext:
Internationellt
Långa amerikanska statsräntor fortsatte upp i går. Den tioåriga räntan är nu mycket nära att bryta över sin högsta notering sedan finanskrisen, vilket den trettioåriga gjorde redan i tisdags. Uppgången skedde trots att inflationen, mätt med Feds favoritmått PCE, kom in lägre än väntat och att marknaden därefter prisar in en något lägre sannolikhet för en räntehöjning i oktober. Långräntorna tog därmed starkare intryck av tillväxtdata som förstärkte bilden av en överraskande robust tillväxt i USA under första halvåret. Aktiemarknaden var något splittrad, där tekniktunga Nasdaq steg något medan S&P 500 backade. För Europas del tyder inflationsdata för enskilda länder på att förväntningen för kärninflationen på 2,5% kan hålla, men det finns viss risk för en överraskning på uppsidan. Fokus flyttas därmed över till tillväxt, där PMI för många länder och ISM för USA står på dagens agenda. På temat Europa rekommenderas läsning av kollegan Pia Fromlets debattartikel i Di om den tyska återhämtningen och dess koppling till svensk industri (betallänk 
här
). I Asien stiger de aktiemarknader som är öppna generellt, men notera att kinesiska marknader är stängda i dag och förblir stängda fram till nästa torsdag på grund av nationaldagsfirandet. Börsterminerna pekar på en negativ öppning i Europa, men en positiv öppning i USA. Oljepriset har under natten fallit kraftigt ner till 97 USD per fat utan att än så länge lämna några stora rubriker. Enligt 
Bloomberg
 rör det sig om att fokus skiftat mot att oljeflödet ut ur mellanöstern börjar närma sig nivåer från innan kriget men frågan är om det även kan finnas kvartalseffekter som påverkar priset. 
Bekräftar USA:s ISM-index för tillverkningsindustrin förra veckans starka PMI?
 Förra veckans överraskande uppgång i PMI-indexen för september, till de högsta nivåerna på flera år, tolkades som ytterligare ett tecken på den amerikanska ekonomins förvånansvärt starka motståndskraft. Vi räknar dock inte med att dagens ISM-index för tillverkningsindustrin, som publiceras kl. 16.00, visar en liknande uppgång. Indexet förväntas i stället vara i stort sett oförändrat, men på fortsatt solida nivåer. En nedgång i flera regionala tillverkningsundersökningar i september utgör dessutom en nedåtrisk. Utöver huvudsiffran kommer ISM-indexet att skärskådas noga för tecken på förnyade flaskhalsar vad gäller priser och leveranstider, i linje med signalerna från både PMI-indexet och vissa regionala index.
Marknadsbokslut för september och tredje kvartalet.
 Nu när både september och tredje kvartalet ligger bakom oss kan vi konstatera att båda perioderna präglats av högre oljepriser och räntor samt en starkare dollar och svagare krona. Amerikanska börsen steg däremot under tredje kvartalet, även om det föll i september (se tabell nedan). En orsak till det kan vara att det framför allt är först i september som den största delen av ränterörelsen skett, vilket också gett upphov till mer utmanande nivåer för aktier. På valutasidan (grafer nedan) har under tredje kvartalet högräntevalutor gynnats medan lågräntevalutor utvecklats svagt – ett tydligt tecken på att så kallade carry trades dominerat. Ett undantag är lågräntevalutan JPY, som fått stöd av upprepade interventioner.
Sverige
Riksbankens protokoll bekräftar den hökaktiga vändningen.
 Protokollet bekräftar den hökaktiga vändningen från förra veckans räntebesked, men visar också att det fortfarande finns olika uppfattningar om riskbalansen inom direktionen. En räntehöjning i november verkar mycket sannolik, och ytterligare höjningar förväntas nästa år. Direktionsledamöterna är dock vaga när det gäller takten och omfattningen av ytterligare höjningar. Den globala utvecklingen kommer att vara avgörande, och energipriserna förblir en viktig faktor för ränteutsikterna. Vi räknar fortfarande med räntehöjningar i november, februari och maj. Läs mer 
här
. 
Återhämtning i svensk PMI för tillverkningsindustrin.
 Kl. 08.30 publiceras PMI för september, och vi tror att indexet kommer att visa en återhämtning. Därmed skulle PMI fortsätta att vända delar av den oväntade nedgången i juli, då indexet sjönk efter en uppåtgående trend sedan 2023.

articles.title: Ahead of September CPI
articles.heading: Norwegian inflation
articles.fulltext:
CPI-ATE expected to continue to edge higher in September
CPI, September , presented October 9
CPI-ATE was far lower than expected in June and July, undershooting in Aug but in line with consensus. The inflation rate in August was 0.3pp below Norges Bank's estimate. Norges Bank lowered the near-term forecast by 0.5pp in the Sep MPR. We see slight upside risks to the near-term estimate. 
Food inflation slowed significantly during the summer and food inflation has turned negative in Sweden (ex-VAT) while Germany is close to zero. The outlook for food prices over the next 12 months is mixed given firmer agricultural commodity prices following higher energy prices and drought in Europe. We predict food inflation to remain around 1.5% in 2027, but uncertainty is high.
Fuel prices are expected to rise by 27 % in September with a normalization of the fuel tax explaining around 60% of the increase. Electricity prices are expected to edge higher.
The outlook over the next 12-18 months is mixed. A stronger NOK is expected to exert downward pressure but high wage inflation contributes to core inflation slowing only gradually. We see slightly higher core inflation than Norges Bank in the near-term, but slightly lower inflation later in 2027.

articles.title: Minutes confirm hawkish shift in September
articles.heading: Riksbank minutes in detail
articles.fulltext:
Key points
Minutes confirm hawkish shift in the Riksbank’s Executive Board, while differences in views on the balance of risks remain within the Board.
A November hike seems very likely, and more tightening is expected next year. However, Board members are vague on the pace and extent of further hikes.
Global developments will be decisive and energy prices remain key for the rate outlook. We expect hikes in November, February and May. 
Minutes confirm our hawkish take on the Monetary Policy Report (MPR) and Governor Thedéen’s press conference last week. 
A November hike seems like a done deal, and more tightening is likely to come unless inflation risks subside more clearly. The extent and pace of tightening is somewhat less certain, with focus centred on the uncertainty surrounding the inflation outlook. The situation in the Middle East will remain key. Policy from other central banks, especially the ECB will also be very important.
Thedéen and Seim both argue clearly for a November hike and explicitly support further tightening next year. Jansson, too, supports the rate forecast and has clearly shifted more hawkishly. Hjelm continues to sound more dovish, arguing that the rate forecast is a bit too high, and highlights that combating a supply driven inflation with rate hikes may come at a high cost. Bunge remains very balanced in her view of the of risks to the rate path.
No Board member seems to argue for more than one hike this year, and all members are rather vague on the extent and timing of further tightening needed. Discussions focus on current inflation risks but also the overall uncertainty on the inflation trajectory. Board members express concern over the weakening of the SEK, highlighting this as a risk for inflation, but as regards further hikes, focus generally lies with supply side shocks and rising demand in the economic recovery.
Policy 
conclusion:
 Overall, the Minutes confirm our view that a November hike is very likely. While the Board’s views vary some on the extent and pace of hikes, all members seem likely to support a near-term hike and some further tightening next year unless the situation changes materially. 
We stick to our forecast for a hike in November, followed by additional hikes in February and May. However, global developments will be decisive and energy prices remain key for the rate outlook. 
Market pricing shifted somewhat to price a higher probability of a November hike than before the publication and 
remains far above both our and the Riksbank's rate projection.
As per usual, we have ranked the individual Board members on our dove-hawk scale.
Hjelm (1)
: Initial situation for the real economy going forward is stronger and more robust. The combination of spare capacity in the labour market and low labour shortages within primarily private services and the retail trade indicates that the labour supply can meet the increased demand as expected. Impact on inflation so far small, except for energy and some indirect effects. The risks to inflation are largely on the upside. After several years of high cyclical unemployment, the forecast shows that normal resource utilisation on the labour market is within reach. However, the cost of using unemployment in the current situation as a means to reduce supply-driven inflation should not be underestimated. Despite the relatively strong driving forces, there is no drama for monetary policy. Given the developments in the forecast, although some probability that the policy rate will need to be raised again during the first half of 2027 seems reasonable.
Bunge (2): 
Overall, this points to an increased risk of higher inflation going forward, which also justifies tighter monetary policy. I think that the policy rate path in the draft report reflects a reasonable trade-off between our main objective of keeping inflation close to 2 per cent and our endeavour to also promote a stable development of the real economy It is important in such a situation (“joint global challenges”) not to be lulled into a false sense of security by inflation being low at present. Overall, I think that it is reasonable to wait and not change the policy rate today but at the same time to clearly communicate that it is likely that the policy rate will be increased before the end of the year. The current policy rate is in my opinion somewhat expansionary and has contributed to supporting the recovery in the Swedish economy.
Jansson (3): 
Supported the decision to revise up the policy rate forecast relatively significantly. The combination of rising demand and supply side constraints and shortages is a dangerous phenomenon. We all remember how inflation rose more or less unchecked in 2022. The situation was unique in many respects, and it is unlikely that it will be repeated in exactly the same way. But today there are similar elements that require vigilance. Although the inflation levels seen in 2022 were exceptional, developments at that time underline how quickly inflation can rise sharply in an adverse scenario. At the same time, measures of short-term price changes – to which I attach quite considerable importance in my monetary policy considerations – have not continued to rise as alarmingly as they did earlier in the summer.
Thedéen (4): 
My assessment today is that it is reasonable to raise the policy rate as early as in November. The forecast for the policy rate next year, which indicates further increases, is also reasonable yet associated with considerable uncertainty. The outlook for economic activity in Sweden is continuing to strengthen. This means that the need to support the recovery no longer exists. At the same time, the supply shocks that were previously pushing up global cost pressures still remain, and once again the earlier futures prices for crude oil, for instance, have proved to be too optimistic. These circumstances, combined with a weak krona, indicate that the risks that inflation will be higher than the target of 2 per cent have increased
. 
Seim (5): 
Since inflationary pressures are higher than normal and the economy is now approaching normal resource utilisation, I consider it appropriate to adjust monetary policy in a tighter direction, in line with the policy rate forecast we present in the draft report. Considered hiking already in September, but after several years of a prolonged economic downturn and persistently high unemployment, I have seen a strong need to wait for reliable signals. The recovery appears robust, but the economy is supported to some extent by subsidies. We are now approaching normal resource utilisation, warranting somewhat tighter monetary policy to achieve inflation at the target over time and a real economy in balance. Unless something happens to overturn my current view of the economic outlook, I will therefore advocate a first policy rate increase at our meeting in November.

articles.title: France - Heading towards the extremes?
articles.heading: Euro area outlook
articles.fulltext:
France risks facing its fourth government crisis in just over two years. The need for substantial savings and growing discontent among opposition parties could bring down Prime Minister Lecornu’s minority government this autumn. Concerns about public finances are reflected in rising French government bond yields. Next year’s presidential election adds to these concerns, as candidates at both ends of the political spectrum gain ground in the polls. A president from the far right or far left would affect not only France, but Europe as a whole.
Key points
Risk of another government crisis
Large fiscal concerns reflected in rising French yields
The presidential election in 2027 adds to these concerns
Major spending cuts in the 2027 budget
The budget for 2027 is due to be submitted to parliament in early October. Under French law, parliament then has 70 days to scrutinise and vote on the proposal. According to Prime Minister Lecornu (from Macron’s Renaissance party), EUR 54 billion in savings will be needed next year to prevent the already large budget deficit from spiralling out of control. Lecornu has also said that the effects of the crisis in the Middle East mean the government will miss its deficit target of 5 per cent of GDP this year, with the deficit potentially reaching 5.4 per cent instead. The aim is to bring the deficit to 5 per cent of GDP in 2027, but according to Lecornu, it could reach as much as 6.5 per cent if no spending cuts are made. Weak GDP growth of 0.6 per cent, according to our latest 
Nordic Outlook
, further complicates the picture. If anything, the risks to that forecast are tilted to the downside.
Weak public finances are driving up interest costs. According to some estimates, these could exceed 3 per cent of GDP in 2028, representing an increase of around 0.25 percentage points per year. This is particularly challenging given Europe’s substantial investment needs, including in defence and infrastructure. With France’s tax-to-GDP ratio already high at 45.3 per cent, the second highest in the EU, there is limited scope to raise taxes to finance new initiatives.
Markets are concerned
The French 10-year government bond yield has risen by more than 100 basis points since 1 July. This partly reflects the global rise in bond yields, but the sharp widening of the spread over its German counterpart also points to a clear French risk premium. This reflects growing concerns about public finances and the fiscal policies that the next president will pursue following the election in April and May 2027. Although candidates have acknowledged the need for fiscal consolidation in various debates, markets appear sceptical, at least about some candidates’ proposals for tackling the country’s large debt burden.
Will the government fall?
Since the snap election in the summer of 2024, France has experienced several government crises. Both Michel Barnier’s and François Bayrou’s governments fell following confidence votes in the parliament after failed budget negotiations. After several confidence votes, Prime Minister Lecornu eventually managed to secure passage of the 2026 budget. The 2027 budget is likely to face at least as much resistance from opposition parties, although the approaching presidential election could encourage them to seek political stability and focus on campaigning instead.
Finding spending cuts that opposition parties would be willing to accept appears difficult. Le Pen, from the far-right National Rally, has said, for example, that her party will not vote for a budget that includes a pension freeze. If Lecornu concludes that the budget lacks parliamentary support, he can invoke Article 49.3 of the constitution to pass it without a parliamentary vote. However, his government could then be brought down by a vote of no confidence. If the budget is delayed, a shutdown of the French government can be avoided by rolling over the 2026 budget into 2027. This would, for example, mean freezing spending, with the exception of pensions, which could in turn add billions in extra costs.
Next year’s presidential election could bring victory for the political extremes
The presidential election will take place in two rounds, on 18 April and 2 May 2027. There is no limit to the number of candidates who can stand in the first round. To qualify, each candidate must secure at least 500 nominations from eligible elected officials. These must come from at least 30 different départements or overseas territories, with no more than 50 from the same area. The president is elected for a five-year term. A candidate who wins an absolute majority in the first round is elected outright, making a second round unnecessary. If no candidate wins an absolute majority in the first round — as has always been the case — the two candidates with the most votes advance to a second round.
The French president has extensive powers, including appointing the prime minister, as well as the president and one-third of the members of the Constitutional Council. The president can also dissolve parliament and serves as commander-in-chief.
Current opinion polls show the strongest first-round support for the far-right candidate Marine Le Pen, at just under 35 per cent. Centrist candidates Édouard Philippe and Gabriel Attal receive 18 and 13 per cent, respectively. The far-left candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon is supported by 16 per cent of respondents. Other prominent potential candidates include Bruno Retailleau, leader of the right-wing Republicans; Raphaël Glucksmann, a member of the European Parliament who is expected to become the candidate of a united left; and François Hollande, a Socialist MP and former president, who has not yet officially announced his candidacy.
The far-left candidate 
Jean-Luc Mélenchon
 has proposed freezing or writing off part of France’s large public debt. However, ECB President Christine Lagarde dismissed the plan as illegal at the press conference following September’s monetary policy decision. Mélenchon also wants to reverse Macron’s pension reform and eventually lower the retirement age to 60. Further increases in the retirement age under the reform have already been suspended until after the presidential election to avert a government collapse; it currently stands at 62 years and nine months. Mélenchon also advocates a higher minimum wage and higher taxes on high earners. He has previously proposed a marginal tax rate of 90 per cent on annual income above EUR 400,000.
Marine Le Pen
, from the far-right National Rally, has pledged that her party would repay the public debt. However, her plans for doing so remain short on detail. Le Pen has spoken of EUR 125 billion in savings and a commitment to a “golden rule” for the budget deficit. According to the limited details available so far, savings would come from government agencies, increased labour force participation among young people, lower contributions to the EU and reduced immigration. At the same time, like Mélenchon, she wants to lower the retirement age: to 62, or to 60 for those with long working careers who started working before the age of 20 and have worked for 42 years. If the crucial pension reform is reversed, it is difficult to see how either the far right or the far left could reduce the high debt burden.
Both centrist candidates, 
Édouard Philippe
 (leader of Horizons, mayor of Le Havre and a former prime minister under Macron) and 
Gabriel Attal
 (leader of Renaissance and another former prime minister under Macron), strongly support fiscal discipline and structural reforms. Philippe has warned against proposals such as Mélenchon’s to freeze or write off part of the debt, arguing that they could shut France out of international financial markets. Attal aims to bring the budget deficit below 3 per cent of GDP by 2032 and balance the budget by 2037.
Although Le Pen currently appears to have an advantage in the polls, the outcome of the second round will depend heavily on which candidates advance from the first. If Le Pen faces either of the centrist candidates, Philippe or Attal, her chances of becoming president would probably diminish. This is because left-wing voters will tend to vote for a centrist candidate to prevent a far-right victory. However, widespread dissatisfaction with the economy could increase support for Le Pen even among left-wing voters. A second round between Le Pen and Mélenchon would probably improve Le Pen’s chances of winning, as centre-left and centre-right voters may consider her a more acceptable alternative to Mélenchon’s far left-wing policies. The winner of the 2027 presidential election therefore looks likely to be the least disliked candidate, rather than necessarily the one with the strongest voter support.
The presidential election matters for Europe
A victory for either candidate from the political extremes could have major consequences for the EU, and particularly for Ukraine. Le Pen wants to halve France’s contributions to the EU and end financial support for Ukraine. She no longer advocates France leaving the EU, instead favouring a transfer of powers from EU institutions back to member states. Mélenchon wants to leave NATO altogether and also demands that the ECB write off part of the public debt. He does not explicitly advocate France leaving the EU but wants to renegotiate EU rules and is prepared to defy them if they obstruct his economic programme. If either centrist candidate becomes the next president, France is likely to remain one of the EU’s main driving forces.

articles.title: US 30-year yield at its highest level since 2002
articles.heading: Nordic Alert
articles.fulltext:
Global key stories
The oil price fell 2.5% to $103.1 per barrel yesterday on signs of increased oil deliveries from the Middle East, contributing to lower European yields. US yields were relatively range-bound during the day, but the 2-year yield fell around 5bp in the evening after Fed President John Williams said that another rate hike towards the end of the year could be appropriate. This contrasts with market pricing, which before his comments implied around 1.5 further hikes by year-end. Further out the curve, however, yields continued to rise, particularly at the very long end. The 30-year yield briefly moved above 5.6%, its highest level since 2002, before yields edged lower towards the end of the session.
The question is how much further the rise in yields can continue.
 US long-term yields are clearly reaching levels that should start to attract more demand – a 30-year inflation-protected bond, for example, currently offers around 3.3% annual real returns. Sooner or later, yields should reach a “critical level” where capital from the equity market starts moving into fixed income – but we are clearly not there yet. The rise in yields is global, putting pressure on highly indebted countries and risking desperate measures to contain borrowing costs. In South Korea, the finance minister warned this morning that the government could buy back its own government bonds, as the US does, in an attempt to limit the bleeding. Such measures do not come without risks, in particular the currency could weaken as a result of such interventions.
The dollar continues to strengthen
 on the back of the relatively sharp rise in US yields. EUR/USD fell to 1.1312 yesterday – its lowest level since May last year – before recovering to 1.1331 this morning. The yen is strengthening against the dollar following fresh Japanese warnings of intervention. The Swedish krona is trading broadly unchanged against the euro over the past 24 hours after a volatile session yesterday, while continuing to weaken against the dollar.
Markets are now turning their attention to today’s US PCE inflation data.
 The Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) will introduce a revised method for calculating the inflation measure, which could contribute 
to a slightly lower inflation rate. Expectations are nevertheless for core inflation to remain at uncomfortably high levels around 3%. In Europe, inflation data from France, Italy and Germany are also due – important ahead of Friday’s composite euro area inflation print. Spanish inflation came in above expectations yesterday. We will also get retail sales data from Sweden and Germany. Today’s Riksbank Minutes will hopefully provide greater insight into the reasoning behind the sharp upward revision to the rate path at last week’s rate decision.
Quarter-end could bring additional market flows.
 Today marks the last day of the month and Q3, which could trigger rebalancing flows across equities, rates and FX. Currency hedges may also need to be adjusted. Our own 
model
 indicates that Swedish portfolio managers have some need to buy SEK and EUR and sell USD.
Nordic key stories
Strongest NIER confidence indicator since 2022.
 The economic outlook continued to 
brighten
 in September, reaching its highest level since 2022, while consumer confidence moved above its historical average for the first time since 2021. Employment plans also improved, although the labour market remains weak. The strong development supports a positive growth outlook, but higher energy prices and mortgage rates could lead to a temporary slowdown in Q4. NIER’s updated forecasts will be published today at 09:00 CET.

articles.title: Amerikanska 30-årsräntan på högsta nivån sedan 2002
articles.heading: Morning Alert
articles.fulltext:
Internationellt
Oljepriset 
föll 2,5% till 103,1 dollar per fat
igår efter tecken på ökade oljeleveranser från Mellanöstern, vilket bidrog till lägre räntor i Europa. Amerikanska räntor handlades relativt sidledes under dagen, men till kvällen sjönk 2-årsräntan omkring 5 punkter efter att Fed-chefen John Williams sagt att det kan vara lämpligt med ytterligare en höjning mot slutet av året. Det står i kontrast till marknadens prissättning, som före talet indikerade omkring 1,5 höjningar till årsskiftet. Längre ut på kurvan fortsatte räntorna däremot att stiga, särskilt i den allra längsta änden. 30-årsräntan var uppe och vände över 5,6%, den högsta nivån sedan 2002, innan räntorna mot kvällen föll tillbaka något.
Frågan är hur mycket längre ränteuppgången kan fortsätta.
 Amerikanska räntor börjar onekligen nå nivåer som bör locka till sig ökad efterfrågan – en 30-årig realindexobligation ger exempelvis omkring 3,3% avkastning per år efter att ha räknat bort inflationen. Förr eller senare stiger räntor till en ”kritisk gräns” där aktiekapital söker sig till räntemarknaden och dämpar uppgången – men vi är uppenbarligen inte där ännu. Ränteuppgången är global och sätter därmed press på högt skuldsatta länder, vilket riskerar att leda till desperata åtgärder för att hålla ned ränteutgifterna. I Sydkorea varnar finansministern under morgonen för att staten kan genomföra återköp av sina egna statsobligationer, såsom USA gör, i ett försök att begränsa blödningen. Denna typ av åtgärder kommer inte utan risker, och inte minst valutan riskerar att försvagas till följd av sådana interventioner.
Dollarn fortsätter att stärkas
 i spåren av den relativt kraftiga ränteuppgången i USA. EUR/USD föll till 1,1312 igår – den lägsta nivån sedan maj förra året – innan den återhämtade sig till 1,1331 under morgonen. Samtidigt stärks yenen mot dollarn efter nya japanska varningar om interventioner. Svenska kronan handlas nära oförändrat mot EUR det senaste dygnet efter en volatil dag igår medan den fortsätter att försvagas mot USD.
Marknaden riktar nu blickarna mot dagens amerikanska PCE-inflation
. Statistikmyndigheten BEA inför reviderade metoder för beräkningen av inflationsmåttet, vilket 
kan bidra
 till att sänka inflationstakten något. Förväntningarna är dock att kärninflationen ligger kvar på obekvämt höga nivåer kring 3 procent. I Europa kommer samtidigt inflationsutfall från Frankrike, Italien och Tyskland – viktiga inför fredagens sammanvägda euroinflation. Gårdagens spanska inflation kom in över förväntningarna. Vi får dessutom detaljhandelssiffror från Sverige och Tyskland. Dagens Riksbanksprotokoll kommer förhoppningsvis ge en tydligare inblick i resonemangen som fördes inför den kraftiga höjningen av räntebanan vid mötet för en vecka sedan. 
Kvartalsslut kan ge extra marknadsflöden.
 Onsdagen för med sig både månadsslut och kvartalsslut, vilket kan ge upphov till omviktningsflöden i aktier, räntor och FX. Även valutasäkringar kan behöva justeras. Vår egen 
modell
 indikerar att svenska portföljförvaltare har ett visst behov att köpa SEK och EUR och sälja USD. 
I dagens 
Ögat
 gör vi en genomgång av ett antal viktiga centralbanker och våra prognosrevideringar. Vi går också igenom läget i Frankrike som riskerar att få sin fjärde regeringskris på två år och där oron för de offentliga finanserna speglas i stigande räntor på franska statspapper. Avslutningsvis avhandlar vi läget inför och möjliga konsekvenser av mellanårsvalet i USA i början av november.
Sverige
Starkaste KI-barometern sedan 2022.
 Konjunkturutsikterna fortsatte att 
ljusna
i september och nådde den högsta nivån sedan 2022, samtidigt som hushållens förtroende steg över det historiska snittet för första gången sedan 2021. Även sysselsättningsplanerna förbättrades, men arbetsmarknaden är fortsatt svag. Den starka utvecklingen stödjer en positiv tillväxtbild, men högre energipriser och bolåneräntor kan ge en tillfällig inbromsning under det fjärde kvartalet. Idag kl. 09.00 publiceras KI:s uppdaterade prognoser.

articles.title: Högre energipriser pressar upp styrräntor
articles.heading: Ögat
articles.fulltext:
Mot bakgrund av högt oljepris, starka tillväxtdata med tillhörande oro för stigande inflation samt centralbankernas senaste beslut och kommunikation har vi reviderat flera styrränteprognoser. Sammantaget räknar vi nu med fler räntehöjningar på kort sikt, bland annat från Fed, ECB, Riksbanken och Bank of England, samtidigt som vi håller fast vid bedömningen att räntorna i flera fall kommer att sänkas i slutet av 2027 och under 2028. 
Frankrike: På väg mot ytterkanterna?
Frankrike riskerar att få sin fjärde regeringskris på lite drygt två år. Stora besparingskrav och ökat missnöje bland oppositionspartierna kan fälla premiärminister Lecornus minoritetsregering i höst. Oro för de offentliga finanserna speglas i stigande räntor på franska statspapper. Presidentvalet nästa år adderar till oron eftersom kandidater på ytterkanterna går starkt framåt i opinionen. En president från ytterhögern eller yttervänstern påverkar inte bara Frankrike, utan hela Europa. 
USA:s mellanårsval: Demokratisk seger blockerar finanspolitiken
Trumps svaga förtroendesiffror i spåren av kriget med Iran och stigande bensinpriser har ökat sannolikheten för demokraterna att ta tillbaka makten över representanthuset. Opinionsmätningarna pekar mot att även senaten kan komma att byta majoritet. Effekterna av en helt eller delvis demokratisk kongress ska inte överdrivas. Trump behåller makten över försvars- och handelspolitiken samt kan lägga veto mot demokratiska reformförslag. Möjligheterna till nya finanspolitiska reformer blockeras dock och demokraterna får större möjlighet till finanspolitisk kohandel kring till exempel försvaret. Tar demokraterna över senaten kan Trump inte utse nya ledamöter till centralbanken Fed eller Högsta domstolen.
